description:
Flip the barrier's demand source from the monolith to the facts, and delete the monolith. Safe because T2's shadow assert already proved all six ExecutableRuntimeDemand fields — including callable_flows, from which latent executables are derived — byte-identical corpus-wide.

## Change
1. Seal gathers `closure.runtime_demands` from the settled `RuntimeDemand(E)` facts (drop the shadow assert and the settle_runtime_demands call).
2. Seal sources latent executables from the gathered `RuntimeDemand(E).callable_flows` (the same demanded_callable_executables rule, now over facts) for its frontier re-entry. Discovery orchestration stays in the seal (deferred to a later epic); only the demand dataflow has moved.

## Why
This is the actual win: the seal stops re-running a whole-closure dataflow on every wake; per-executable jobs re-derive only on neighbor ascent. The barrier stays byte-identical, so transport/materialize/abi/... are untouched.

## Rip out (verified single-caller, all in jobs/runtime_demand.rs)
- `settle_runtime_demands` (the two nested loops)
- `base_return_demand` (re-expressed as contributions in T2)
- `propagate_call_return_demands` (now the per-E ReturnDemand contribution)
- `apply_callable_boundary_return_demands` (now the per-E boundary-return contribution)
- the shadow `assert_eq!` and any shadow-only plumbing
The three transfer functions (derive_executable_runtime_demand, collect_executable_facts, derive_callable_flow_facts) STAY — now called only by DeriveRuntimeDemand(E).

## Check
`cargo test --lib` + `tests/fixture_matrix.rs` green (barrier unchanged → goldens unchanged). Seal-run telemetry on enum_take_drop_split drops from ~538 to single digits; no whole-closure clone per wake. Update the relevant .agent/docs and northstar/seal narrative to describe demand as per-executable facts. Zero warnings; no scaffolding left behind.
title: Runtime demand: cut the seal over to the facts and strangle the monolith
